name: Manombai
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.note: Alternate names Aru, Manobai, Wamar, Wokam; only Collins 1982 and Hughes 1987 as modern references; no descriptive (grammar/phonology) reference; no stress info.

sources.citation: Daigle, Benjamin. 2015. A grammar sketch of Batuley: an Austronesian language of Aru, eastern Indonesia. MA thesis, Leiden University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Different Aru language (Batuley, batu1263), not Manombai. Sec. 2.6.1 p. 30: 'Stress is phonemic in Batuley. Although stress most often falls on the penultimate syllable of a word, it is not entirely predictable.' Manombai appears only as the neighbouring language of Kobamar village; no Manombai stress data.

sources.citation: Schapper, Antoinette. 2015. Neuter gender in the languages of Aru. Wacana 16(1).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only recent comparative paper citing Manombai data (from Nivens/Hughes fieldnotes); may carry a footnote on Aru stress; could not be opened (an automated-access block).

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 1987. The languages of Kei, Tanimbar and Aru: a lexicostatistic classification. NUSA 27: 71-111.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 2.2.3.7 'Wokam (also known as the Manombai Language)': c. 5,700 speakers, 21 villages on Wokam/Kobror/Maikor Is; only reliable wordlist from Benjina (Kobror I.); the Wangel (Wamar I.) list was rejected as unreliable; 'Dialect survey will need to be conducted'. Lexicostatistics only, no phonology.

sources.citation: von Rosenberg, C. B. H. 1867. Reis naar de Zuidoostereilanden, gedaan in 1865 op last der regering van Nederlandsch-Indië. 's Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff. (Bijlage A, Vergelijkende woordenlijst incl. 'Wammer' = Manombai)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Wordlist preface (p. 107): French accents used for e-quality, breve/macron for short/long syllables, g as in German; nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Earl, George Windsor. 1853. The Native Races of the Indian Archipelago: Papuans. London: Hippolyte Bailliere.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic overview of the Arru Islands (pp. 93 ff.); no language description, no stress.

sources.citation: Earl, George Windsor. 1848. Specimens of the dialects of Timor and of the chain of islands extending thence to New Guinea. Journal of the Indian Archipelago and Eastern Asia 2: 695-704.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative wordlist (Arru column); introduction discusses Kisar gutturals only; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Brumund, J. F. G. 1844. Proeve over de Aroe-taal. Tijdschrift voor Neêrland's Indië 6(2): 321-340.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress placement. The only first-hand description of the language (speech of Wokkam village on Wokam I. and of Durdjella and Wangil on Wammer/Wamar I.). Pp. 328-329 describe the language as vowel-rich, 'vloeijend, welluidend', with elision/contraction; pp. 332-333 'Eenige opmerkingen ten dienste der uitspraak' give only vowel-quality diacritics (è, o, é: 'é moet krachtig gehoord worden, gelijk alle vocalen, zoo zij niet tusschen consonanten staan'), a syllable-separating mark, and Ujir variants. No klemtoon/accent rule anywhere in the 20 pages.
Nothing on phonology; cites only Hughes 1987 and Ethnologue/Glottolog.

sources.citation: Nivens, Richard (SIL). Unpublished Aru survey materials / Proto-Aru database (Toolbox files, from 1987 fieldwork), incl. Manombai wordlists; cited as 'Nivens (n.d.) on Aru as a whole' in Schapper 2015 and listed on OLAC for woo.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern phonetic transcriptions of Manombai likely to mark stress; SIL Aru survey may include a phonology note per language.
